title: Favorite drummers, his brother, and Barney Bigard
summary: He rates his brother as a good nightclub drummer and says Barney Bigard only became a musician after leaving New Orleans for Duke Ellington.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Who were your favorite drummers? I suppose your brother would be one of them, but who else?

No, I wouldn't say that. You wouldn't rank him as the best or anything then, huh? No, he's a good drummer because he's a regular nightclub man, you know? Yeah. And, uh... Because he played with all the different fellas I'm telling you about. Jimmy Noon. Uh... Uh... Alvin Nicholas. And I wouldn't say Bonabigo because Bonabigo had come in on the last.
He was just learning, I guess, huh?

Yeah, and, uh... He learned. He learned. And when he got a good foothold, then he left away from here. That's when he was a musician and when he left here. Yeah. I don't know... Somebody told me he was playing with Duke, was it?
Well, yeah. He played with him, I think, 13 years. Wow. A long time. He just quit him about 1940. He went with him in the 20s.
Well that's when he got to be a musician when he left here. He wasn't much when he was here in New Orleans.
And he played with Joe Oliver up in Chicago too, I know.
